name: Centro
tagline: The wide avenues and the central market
description: The core of the city along Avenida Afonso Pena, one of the broadest urban avenues in Brazil, with the central market where the Okinawan soba is served, the shops and the older apartment stock. It is flat, walkable and where most of the city's history sits.
bestFor: Anyone wanting to walk to the market and the shops
pros: The central market and its soba stalls
Flat and walkable along Afonso Pena

name: Jardim dos Estados
tagline: The leafy district along the avenue
description: An established residential neighbourhood east of the centre along Afonso Pena, with tree-lined streets, older houses and apartment blocks, and the Parque das Nacoes Indigenas at its eastern end. It is the most pleasant central district to live in.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting shade, parks and a central position

name: Chacara Cachoeira
tagline: The newest towers and the best restaurants
description: The district east of the park where most of the city's new apartment towers have gone up, along with its best restaurants, bars and the shopping centres. It is where the professional population has moved and where infrastructure is most reliable.
bestFor: Anyone wanting a new flat with reliable services
pros: The best restaurants and bars in the city
Close to the park and the shopping centres
cons: The most expensive rents in Campo Grande

name: Vila Planalto
tagline: The government district by the state park
description: The area around the Parque dos Poderes, where the state government buildings sit in open parkland with capybaras on the lawns and monkeys in the trees. Residential streets nearby are quiet, green and unusually pleasant for a capital district.
bestFor: Anyone wanting quiet, green surroundings and wildlife nearby
pros: Close to the newer commercial district
cons: A vehicle is needed for most things
Quiet to the point of empty at weekends

name: Universitario
tagline: The campus district south of the centre
description: The area around the federal university campus in the south of the city, with student housing, cheap food and the cheapest rents in the developed part of Campo Grande. The campus itself is large and wooded and open to walk through.
bestFor: Budget stays and anyone with university business
pros: The cheapest rents in the city
Large wooded campus to walk in
